neighbours.label: ' to' used as a preposition (towards / compared to / to oneself), not the infinitive marker
fire: His working style is very different to that of his father.
The children ran over and waved to the bus driver.
She sang quietly to herself while painting the fence.
We talked to the neighbours about the broken gate.
This version is similar to the one we bought last year.
He handed the keys to the new tenant on Monday.
The old road leads to a small fishing village.
They explained the rules to every new player.
quiet: His working style made it hard to keep up with his father.
The children ran over and wanted to greet the bus driver.
She decided to paint the fence quietly by herself.
We hoped to fix the broken gate before the neighbours saw.
We plan to buy this version again next year.
He forgot to hand over the keys on Monday.
The old road is easy to miss near the fishing village.
They tried to explain the rules more clearly this time.

notes: near misses keep ' to' but as the infinitive marker.
